R196.note: Correctly enables @EnableMethodSecurity and adds resource-level checks, but the security service invents a new authorization policy beyond the original ADMIN-only intent (allows non-admin self-delete; blocks admin self-suspend that was previously permitted) - disclosed but not required by the finding.

R197.note: EvalSymlinks on both base and full path with prefix check correctly closes the symlink escape while still reading legitimate in-directory files; minor undisclosed shift of error type (ErrPermission instead of not-exist) for missing files is immaterial since the request fails either way.

R198.note: Moves the state-changing delete behind @PostMapping so Spring Security's CsrfFilter validates it, closing the GET-triggered CSRF gap; the new GET confirmation view is disclosed, though it relies on an unverified view resolver/template not otherwise evidenced in this REST-only app.

R199.note: Build FAILs: SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler is not a real Spring Security class (Spring's own migration guide has developers write this class themselves) - the fix as written does not compile, silently breaking the whole app including legitimate requests.

R200.note: Standard normalize+resolve+startsWith containment check correctly blocks traversal while preserving the original path for legitimate filenames and existing exception handling.

R201.note: Replaces raw inline-protocol socket writes with StackExchange.Redis's parameterized StringSet, which serializes key/value via RESP length-prefixing so embedded CRLF cannot break out - the appropriate, named-library fix for this sink.

R202.note: Tika magic-byte detection plus allowlist correctly replaces the forgeable content-type header check; the additional ImageIO re-encode (openly stated) strips metadata/re-compresses as an intentional anti-polyglot measure without blocking legitimate uploads.

R203.note: Path.GetRelativePath-based containment (rejecting '..' prefixes and rooted results) correctly closes the sibling-directory string-prefix bypass while passing legitimate in-directory files through unchanged.

R204.note: Replaces Math.random() with SecureRandom-backed 128-bit tokens, Base64-encoded; the resulting token format differs from the original digit string but this is the intended, disclosed fix and downstream code only stores/compares the string opaquely.
